rows.note: This is the all-purpose term for a person who guides guests to their seats at a church, cinema, or similar venue.

example.english: Before the show, the usher told us to turn off our phones and led us to our seats.
example.traditional: 入場前，帶位員叫我哋熄手機，跟住帶我哋入座。
example.jyutping: jap6 coeng4 cin4 daai3 wai6 jyun4 giu3 ngo5 dei6 sik1 sau2 gei1 gan1 zyu6 daai3 ngo5 dei6 jap6 zo6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when staff guide customers or audience members to their seats.

example.english: The waiter will usher us to our seats when the wedding banquet starts.
example.traditional: 婚宴開始喇，侍應生帶位我哋入座。
example.jyutping: fan1 jin3 hoi1 ci2 laa3 si6 jing3 saang1 daai3 wai2 ngo5 dei6 jap6 zo6

rows.note: Use this when the emphasis is on accompanying someone rather than taking them to a particular seat.

example.english: Can you usher me through the hospital visit so I won't be so scared?
example.traditional: 你陪住我去見醫生，我就冇咁驚。
example.jyutping: nei5 pui4 zyu6 ngo5 heoi3 gin3 ji1 saang1 ngo5 zau6 mou5 gam3 geng1

rows.note: Use this specifically for the male attendant or escort in a wedding party, not for a seat guide.

example.english: Before the wedding started, the usher helped the groom straighten his tie.
example.traditional: 婚禮開始前，伴郎幫新郎整理好領呔。
example.jyutping: fan1 lai5 hoi1 ci2 cin4 bun6 long2 bong1 san1 long2 zing2 lei5 hou2 leng5 taai1
